title: Ethiopian Capital Markets Law and Regulation
subtitle: ECMA, licensing, public offers, market conduct and enforcement, from first principles to a listing roadmap
summary: Learn the rules that govern Ethiopia's capital market, then apply them to a bank with 15,000 shareholders that sets up an investment bank and lists on the Ethiopian Securities Exchange.
audience: Compliance, legal and operations staff of capital market service providers, issuers and banks (foundational modules); compliance officers, legal counsel, senior managers and board members of licensed firms (advanced modules). Learners should first complete Introduction to Capital Markets, Level 1, or have equivalent knowledge.
objectives: Describe ECMA's mandate, powers and structure and the scope of Capital Market Proclamation No. 1248/2021
Name the license categories and the core obligations of licensed persons
Explain the rules on public offers, disclosure and prohibited market conduct
Build and run a compliance program for a licensed capital market firm
Advise issuers on offer, listing and continuing obligations, including existing unlisted share companies
Analyze enforcement cases and the interplay of ECMA, NBE and Commercial Code rules

runningCase.name: Bank A and Bank A Capital
runningCase.text: Bank A S.C. is a fictional Ethiopian commercial bank founded in 2009. It has about 15,000 shareholders, paid-up capital of Birr 6 billion, shareholders' equity of Birr 7.6 billion and total capital of Birr 8 billion, and its shares have changed hands only through its own share register, never on an exchange. The board has approved two projects: setting up Bank A Capital S.C., a wholly owned investment bank with Birr 150 million of capital, and listing Bank A on the ESX Main Board while raising Birr 2 billion of new capital. Chief compliance officer Hirut Alemayehu and legal counsel Dawit Gebremedhin must map every approval from ECMA, the ESX and the NBE. Each module takes the case one step further, from the legal framework to the final compliance timeline.

modules.title: The legal framework and ECMA
modules.summary: See how the Capital Market Proclamation, ECMA directives and the ESX Rulebook fit together, what counts as a security, and how ECMA licenses, supervises and sanctions.
objectives: Describe the objectives and scope of Capital Market Proclamation No. 1248/2021
Place proclamations, directives and exchange rules in the Ethiopian legal hierarchy
Recognize a security and a capital market activity in everyday situations
Explain ECMA's powers and the route from an ECMA decision to the Capital Market Tribunal
Identify where company, banking, AML and investment law meet capital market law

lessons.title: Why Ethiopia has a capital market law
body: For decades Ethiopian companies raised long-term money from bank loans and from selling shares privately to founders, friends and customers. There was no regulator for securities, no exchange and no rules on what an issuer had to disclose. Many share companies, including banks and insurers, ended up with thousands of shareholders and no market where those shares could be priced and traded.

Capital Market Proclamation No. 1248/2021, adopted in June 2021 as part of the Home-Grown Economic Reform program, changed that. It created the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority (ECMA), set the rules for securities exchanges, service providers, public offers and market abuse, and gave ECMA the power to write detailed directives. The Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX) began trading on 10 January 2025.

The law has one central idea: investors who hand money to issuers and intermediaries must get fair treatment, honest information and a market that is not rigged. Every rule in this course serves that idea.

example.title: Two kinds of share sale
example.text: In 2015, Mekdes Haile bought 20 shares in a new insurance share company from a sales agent at a church gathering in Bahir Dar. She received a share certificate and no prospectus, and selling her shares later meant finding a buyer herself. Today, a company offering shares to the public must register the offer with ECMA, publish a prospectus and, if it lists, report to investors through the ESX. The same Birr 20,000 now buys a protected position.

lessons.tip: When a question arises, start with the proclamation, then the directive, then the exchange rule: the answer is usually in that order of detail.

lessons.title: The legal hierarchy
body: Ethiopian capital market rules sit in layers. The Constitution is at the top. Proclamations passed by Parliament come next: the Capital Market Proclamation, the Commercial Code, the Banking Business Proclamation and others. Council of Ministers regulations can add detail where a proclamation calls for them.

Below these are ECMA directives, issued under the directive power in Article 108 of the proclamation. They carry the detail: licensing categories, capital, fees, offer documents. At the base are the rules of self-regulating bodies such as the ESX Rulebook, which ECMA approves and which bind exchange members and listed issuers.
A lower rule cannot override a higher one. If an exchange rule conflicts with a directive, the directive prevails; if a directive conflicts with the proclamation, the proclamation prevails.

scenario.title: A rule that does not fit
scenario.situation: A broker's operations head, Yonas Tadesse, reads an ESX trading procedure that seems to allow a practice an ECMA directive forbids. His sales team wants to follow the exchange procedure because it is more recent.
scenario.question: Which rule should the broker follow?
options: The ECMA directive, because a directive ranks above an exchange rule
The ESX procedure, because it is more recent
scenario.explain: Exchange rules sit below ECMA directives. The broker follows the directive and raises the conflict with the ESX and ECMA; the date of the rule does not change its rank.

regulation.source: Capital Market Proclamation No. 1248/2021, Articles 35 to 38 and 108
regulation.text: Article 108 empowers ECMA to issue directives to implement the proclamation. Articles 35 to 38 deal with securities exchange rules, which is the basis on which the ESX Rulebook operates under ECMA oversight.

lessons.title: What counts as a security and a capital market activity
body: The proclamation defines securities broadly. Shares and bonds are the obvious ones, but units in a collective investment scheme, rights to subscribe for shares and other investment instruments also count. The test is substance, not the label: if people put money into a common pool expecting a return from someone else's efforts, the arrangement may well be a security whatever it is called.

A capital market activity is a business of dealing with securities for others or for oneself as a market professional: brokering, dealing, underwriting, giving investment advice, managing portfolios, operating a fund, holding client securities in custody or rating issuers. Doing any of these as a business needs an ECMA license.

example.title: The coffee export pool
example.text: Abel Mulugeta, a coffee trader in Hawassa, invited 400 neighbors to buy 'membership certificates' at Birr 5,000 each in a coffee export pool he would manage, promising a share of export profits. He called it a cooperative, but the members do no work and rely only on his efforts. A compliance officer reading this sees a collective investment arrangement offered to the public, which brings it within capital market law.

scenario.title: Is it a security?
scenario.situation: A real estate developer in Addis Ababa sells 'investment slots' of Birr 250,000 to 80 people. Each slot pays a quarterly share of rental income from a building the developer manages; slot holders have no say in management.
scenario.question: How should a compliance officer first treat these slots?
options: As a simple property sale outside capital market law
As a bank deposit under NBE rules
As a possible security, since investors pool money and rely on the developer's efforts for returns
As a loan to the developer that needs no review
scenario.explain: Pooled money and returns that depend on another person's efforts are the hallmarks of an investment arrangement. It needs legal review under the proclamation before more slots are sold.

lessons.title: ECMA's mandate, board and powers
body: ECMA is the regulator of the whole capital market. It is governed by a board and run by a director general and staff. Its mandate is to develop a fair, efficient and transparent market and to protect investors.

Its powers follow the life of a market participant: it licenses exchanges and service providers, registers public offers, supervises through reports and inspections, investigates suspected breaches, imposes administrative sanctions and writes directives. It also recognizes self-regulatory organizations and approves exchange rules. ECMA collects fees for licenses, offers and transactions, set in its Fee Directive No. 996/2024.

regulation.text: The directive sets ECMA's fees. Examples: a broker pays ETB 60,000 to apply, ETB 132,000 for the license and ETB 66,000 a year to renew. A share offer pays ETB 300,000 plus 0.1% of the value offered; a bond offer ETB 150,000 plus 0.05%. Transaction fees are 0.15% of value for shares and 0.005% for fixed income.

worked.title: Bank A: ECMA fee for registering a Birr 2 billion share offer

rows.label: As a share of the amount raised

worked.note: The ECMA fee is modest beside the raise, but it belongs in the offer budget alongside adviser, audit, printing and ESX costs.

lessons.title: Enforcement, the Capital Market Tribunal and appeals
body: When ECMA suspects a breach it can demand documents, inspect premises and records, and investigate. If it finds a breach it can warn, fine, suspend or revoke a license, or order a firm to correct its conduct. Serious offenses, such as market abuse, can also carry criminal liability under the proclamation.

Decisions must be fair and reviewable. The proclamation establishes a Capital Market Tribunal to hear appeals against ECMA decisions, so a sanctioned firm or person can challenge a decision before an independent body, with further review in the courts as the law provides. The proclamation also provides for investor compensation arrangements to protect clients when a licensed firm fails.

example.title: A broker's late client statements
example.text: Sunrise Securities S.C., a fictional broker in Addis Ababa, sent client statements months late and could not reconcile client cash. ECMA inspectors documented the gaps, heard the firm's explanation and imposed a fine with an order to fix its reconciliation within a set period. The firm accepted the order rather than appeal because its own records confirmed the findings.

scenario.title: Challenging a suspension
scenario.situation: Meron Bekele, managing director of a fictional investment adviser, believes ECMA suspended her firm's license without considering documents she submitted after the inspection.
scenario.question: What is the proper route?
options: Keep advising clients until a court rules
Ask the NBE to overturn the suspension
Transfer the clients to an unlicensed affiliate
Appeal the decision to the Capital Market Tribunal, setting out the documents ECMA did not consider
scenario.explain: ECMA decisions are challenged before the Capital Market Tribunal. Continuing to operate breaches the suspension, the NBE has no role in ECMA licensing, and an unlicensed affiliate cannot take the business.

lessons.title: Where capital market law meets other laws
body: Capital market law does not stand alone. The Commercial Code (reported as Proclamation No. 1243/2021) governs how share companies are formed, issue shares and hold general meetings. Banking law decides what a bank and its subsidiaries may do. AML/CFT law sets customer due diligence duties for every licensed firm. The Investment Proclamation and FX rules decide what foreign and diaspora investors may buy and how money moves.

A compliance officer must read these together. A bank that lists its shares needs ECMA and ESX approvals for the offer and listing, Commercial Code steps for the share issue, and NBE rules on who may own significant stakes. A bank that forms a broker or investment bank needs both an NBE approval and an ECMA license.

example.title: Bank A's two projects, two sets of regulators
example.text: Hirut Alemayehu, Bank A's chief compliance officer, listed the authorities for the board. Bank A Capital S.C., the planned investment bank, needs NBE approval for the bank's investment and an ECMA license. The listing and Birr 2 billion raise need a general meeting resolution under the Commercial Code, ECMA registration of the offer, ESX listing approval and NBE approval for any investor reaching a significant stake. The board saw at once that one project manager could not run both alone.

regulation.text: All sectors are open to foreign investors unless a regulation reserves them, and the law guarantees remittance of profits and capital. Foreign participation in listed Ethiopian securities is expected to be set by ECMA's Foreign Portfolio Investment Regulation, posted as a draft on 29 September 2026; check its final text before advising foreign clients.

takeaways: Proclamation No. 1248/2021 created ECMA and the legal base for the ESX, licensing, public offers and market abuse rules.
Rules rank in order: Constitution, proclamations, regulations, ECMA directives under Article 108, then exchange and SRO rules.
Substance decides whether something is a security: pooled money with returns from another's efforts is a warning sign.
ECMA licenses, registers, supervises, investigates and sanctions; its decisions can be appealed to the Capital Market Tribunal.
Capital market questions often also involve the Commercial Code, banking law, AML/CFT law and investment law.

quiz.q: Which article of Proclamation No. 1248/2021 gives ECMA its directive power?
quiz.explain: Article 108 empowers ECMA to issue directives implementing the proclamation.

quiz.q: An ESX rule conflicts with an ECMA directive. Which applies?
quiz.explain: Exchange rules rank below ECMA directives.

quiz.q: Which arrangement is most likely a security?
options: A loan from a friend repaid in fixed installments
Buying a car for personal use
Certificates sold to 300 people giving a share of profits from a business they do not run
quiz.explain: Pooled money with returns from someone else's efforts is the hallmark of an investment security.

quiz.q: Where does a firm appeal an ECMA sanction?
quiz.explain: The proclamation establishes the Capital Market Tribunal to hear appeals against ECMA decisions.

quiz.q: What is the ECMA fee for registering a Birr 500 million share offer under Directive No. 996/2024?
quiz.explain: ETB 300,000 plus 0.1% of 500 million (ETB 500,000) equals ETB 800,000.

quiz.q: A bank wants to set up a broker subsidiary. Whose approval does it need?
options: Neither, if the bank owns all the shares
Both the NBE, for the bank's investment, and ECMA, for the license
quiz.explain: Banking law governs the bank's investment and capital market law governs the license.

modules.title: Licensing capital market service providers
modules.summary: Learn the license categories and minimum capital under Directive No. 980/2024, the people a licensed firm must have, how licensing and renewal work, and the duties that come with a license.
objectives: Name the main license categories under Directive No. 980/2024 and their minimum capital
Explain the cash capital, liquid asset and representative requirements
Describe the application, licensing and annual renewal steps and fees
List the core obligations of a licensed person
Apply NBE investment rules to a bank that owns a capital market firm

lessons.title: Who needs a license
body: Directive No. 980/2024 governs the licensing and supervision of capital market service providers and sets 15 license categories. Each category matches an activity: an investment bank underwrites and advises on offers, a broker executes client orders, a dealer trades on its own account, an investment adviser gives recommendations, a portfolio manager manages client money, a custodian holds client assets, a fund operator runs collective investment schemes and a credit rating agency rates issuers.

The license follows the activity, not the job title. A person who regularly advises others on which securities to buy, for a fee, is giving investment advice whether or not they call themselves an adviser. Before launching any service, a compliance officer maps it to a category and checks that the firm holds that license.

example.title: The engineer who advised his colleagues
example.text: Natnael Girma, a civil engineer in Adama, studied the ESX listings and began charging colleagues Birr 1,500 a month for weekly stock picks. After 60 people joined, a friend in compliance pointed out that regular paid recommendations are investment advice, a licensed activity. Natnael stopped charging and is now studying for a license with a licensed adviser firm.

lessons.title: Minimum capital by category
body: Directive No. 980/2024 sets minimum paid-up capital by category, scaled to the risk each activity carries. Firms that hold client assets or underwrite offers need the most. An investment bank within a banking group needs Birr 100 million and a standalone investment bank Birr 25 million; a custodian Birr 100 million; a collective investment scheme operator Birr 25 million; a credit rating agency and a portfolio manager Birr 15 million each; a dealer Birr 10 million; a broker Birr 6 million; a digital sub-broker Birr 1 million; and an investment adviser from Birr 100,000 to Birr 500,000.

Capital must be paid in cash. A building, software or a shareholder's promise does not count. A licensed firm must also keep liquid assets of at least 40% of its total assets, so that capital stays available to absorb losses rather than being tied up in fixed assets.

scenario.title: Capital in kind
scenario.situation: Founders of Meskel Square Brokers S.C. have Birr 4 million in cash and offer an office floor valued at Birr 3 million as the rest of their capital for a broker license.
scenario.question: What should their adviser tell them?
options: The license can be granted because the total is Birr 7 million
Capital must be paid in cash, so they need at least Birr 6 million in cash
A broker needs no minimum capital
They should apply as a dealer instead
scenario.explain: Directive No. 980/2024 requires capital paid in cash. The office floor does not count, and a dealer license would need Birr 10 million.

regulation.source: ECMA Directive No. 980/2024, Licensing and supervision of capital market service providers
regulation.text: Sets 15 license categories and minimum capital from Birr 100,000 (individual adviser) to Birr 100 million (investment bank within a banking group, custodian). Capital must be paid in cash, liquid assets must be at least 40% of total assets, and licenses are renewed annually.

lessons.title: People: representatives and the chief compliance officer
body: A license is granted to a firm, but it is the people who serve clients. Directive No. 980/2024 requires at least three appointed representatives, including a licensed chief compliance officer. Representatives must themselves be fit and proper: competent, honest and financially sound.

The chief compliance officer is the firm's internal guardian. The role needs independence from sales and trading, direct access to the board and enough authority to stop a transaction. A firm that makes its top salesperson the compliance officer has a license on paper but no compliance function in practice.
points: At least three appointed representatives
One of them a licensed chief compliance officer
Fit and proper: competence, integrity, financial soundness
Changes in key persons notified to ECMA

example.title: Bank A Capital's first hires
example.text: Bank A Capital S.C. planned a lean start, but Hirut Alemayehu insisted on three appointed representatives from day one: a head of corporate finance, a head of brokerage and Selamawit Desta as licensed chief compliance officer reporting to the board's audit committee. The ECMA application went in with all three named, which avoided a request for more information.

scenario.title: Two hats
scenario.situation: To save costs, the board of a new fictional broker proposes that its head of sales, Bereket Asfaw, also serve as chief compliance officer. He is licensed and very experienced.
scenario.question: What is the best advice to the board?
options: Accept, since he is licensed and experienced
Appoint a separate chief compliance officer who reports to the board and is independent of sales
Leave the compliance role vacant until the firm is profitable
scenario.explain: A compliance officer who also runs sales would be checking his own targets. The function needs independence and a direct line to the board.

lessons.title: The application, license and annual renewal
body: A service provider first forms its company and obtains commercial registration, then applies to ECMA with its business plan, proof of cash capital, ownership details, fit and proper documents for directors and representatives, and its policies and systems. ECMA reviews the file, may inspect premises and systems, and grants the license on payment of the license fee.

Licenses are renewed annually. Renewal is not automatic: ECMA looks at the year's conduct, returns and capital. Firms should start the renewal file well before the expiry date and budget for the renewal fee.

lessons.title: Core obligations of a licensed person
body: A license brings continuing duties. The firm must keep its capital and liquid assets above the minimum, keep client money and securities separate from its own, act honestly and in the client's interest, manage conflicts of interest, keep proper records, and send ECMA its periodic returns and notices.
These duties apply every day, not only at renewal. A firm that meets its capital on licensing day but lets liquid assets fall below 40% six months later is in breach, even if no one has noticed yet.

example.title: A dealer's growing desk
example.text: Lalibela Dealers S.C., a fictional dealer, kept buying unlisted shares for its own book. Its capital stayed above Birr 10 million, but unlisted holdings are hard to sell and liquid assets fell to 35% of total assets. The chief compliance officer flagged the breach to the board, which sold part of the book and reported the issue to ECMA.

lessons.title: Bank-owned capital market firms
body: Banks are natural owners of investment banks and brokers: they have clients, branches and capital. Banking law limits what a bank may invest in, however. SBB/92/2024 sets the investment limits for banks and allows a bank to own up to 100% of a capital market service provider with NBE prior approval. The bank may not act as a capital market service provider itself, and it may not hold equity in a credit rating agency.

So a bank-owned investment bank needs two approvals: the NBE for the bank's investment and ECMA for the license. The higher Birr 100 million capital for an investment bank within a banking group reflects the larger client base and potential conflicts in such groups.

scenario.title: Selling in the branches
scenario.situation: Bank A wants its 120 branch tellers to sell Bank A Capital's investment products to depositors and to recommend which shares to buy, before Bank A Capital is licensed.
scenario.question: What should compliance advise?
options: Go ahead, since the tellers are bank staff
Let tellers advise only diaspora clients
Ask the NBE to license the tellers
Wait for the license, and even then let only licensed representatives give investment advice; tellers may refer clients
scenario.explain: Investment advice is a licensed activity done through licensed representatives. Tellers can refer clients, but they cannot advise, and nothing can be offered before the license is granted.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/92/2024, Limits on bank investments
regulation.text: A bank may invest at most 5% in a single insurer, 10% in any other single non-bank business, 15% of total capital in all non-bank equity, and 10% in real estate. It may own up to 100% of a capital market service provider with NBE prior approval, but may not act as one itself or hold equity in a credit rating agency.

Total non-bank equity after the investment

worked.note: Even counted in the aggregate, the investment fits. Bank A still needs NBE approval to own 100% of Bank A Capital, and Bank A Capital needs Birr 100 million minimum as a group investment bank, which its Birr 150 million covers.

takeaways: Directive No. 980/2024 sets 15 license categories; the activity, not the job title, decides which license is needed.
Minimum capital ranges from Birr 100,000 for an adviser to Birr 100 million for a group investment bank or custodian, paid in cash.
Liquid assets must stay at or above 40% of total assets every day, not only on licensing day.
Every firm needs at least three appointed representatives, including an independent, licensed chief compliance officer.
A bank may own up to 100% of a capital market firm with NBE approval under SBB/92/2024, and the firm still needs its own ECMA license.

quiz.explain: A broker needs Birr 6 million; a dealer needs Birr 10 million.

modules.title: Public offers, market conduct and AML/CFT
modules.summary: Know when an offer needs ECMA registration and a prospectus, recognize insider dealing, manipulation and conflicts, apply AML/CFT due diligence, and classify activities as permitted, licensable or prohibited.
objectives: Explain when an offer is public and what registration and a prospectus require
Distinguish a private placement from a public offer using the 100 investor ceiling
Recognize insider dealing, market manipulation and false statements
Apply client asset segregation and conflict rules
Carry out customer due diligence and beneficial ownership checks

lessons.title: When an offer becomes public
body: An offer of securities to the public must be registered with ECMA before it is made, with a prospectus approved for publication. ECMA's public offer and trading directive (reported as No. 1030/2024) sets the registration process, prospectus content, exemptions and ongoing reporting.

The main exemption is the private placement: an offer made to a limited group, reported as at most 100 investors. Above that ceiling, the offer is treated as public whatever the issuer calls it. Splitting one offer into several 'private' rounds to stay under the ceiling defeats the rule and invites enforcement.

example.title: Ethio telecom's 2024 share offer
example.text: Ethio telecom's 2024 share offer, sold to the public through the telebirr app, showed how a large retail offer can reach millions of Ethiopians digitally. It also showed why registration matters: retail buyers need a clear document on price, rights, risks and how to sell later.

scenario.title: Selling bank shares to 150 people
scenario.situation: A fictional bank under formation, through its organizing committee, plans to sell shares to 150 founders and friends in Dire Dawa without a prospectus, calling it a private placement.
scenario.question: How should the offer be classified?
options: A private placement, because the buyers are friends
Outside capital market law, because banks answer only to the NBE
A public offer that must be registered with ECMA, because it exceeds the 100 investor ceiling
Permitted if split into two rounds of 75
scenario.explain: 150 investors exceeds the reported 100 investor ceiling for private placements. Splitting the offer to avoid the rule is itself a problem, and the NBE's role does not remove ECMA's.

regulation.source: ECMA public offer and trading directive (reported as No. 1030/2024; text to confirm)
regulation.text: Covers registration of public offers with ECMA, prospectus content, exemptions including private placements to no more than 100 investors, and ongoing reporting by issuers. The number and ceiling are reported in the programme register; confirm them against the official text.

lessons.title: What a prospectus must tell investors
body: The prospectus is the issuer's promise of full and fair disclosure. It explains the business, the risks, how the money will be used, the audited financial statements, the directors and major shareholders, the offer price and terms, and the rights attached to the securities.
After the offer, the issuer's duty continues: ongoing reports keep investors informed. ECMA charges a registration fee on each offer under Directive No. 996/2024.

items.label: Risk factors
items.text: What could go wrong, specific to the issuer

items.label: Use of proceeds
items.text: Where the money goes

items.label: Financial statements
items.text: Audited accounts and key figures

items.label: Directors and owners
items.text: Who runs and controls the issuer

items.label: Offer terms
items.text: Price, size, timetable, allocation

items.label: Rights of holders
items.text: Votes, dividends, transfer

example.title: A vague use of proceeds
example.text: A draft prospectus for the fictional Tana Agro-Processing S.C. said the Birr 400 million raised would be used 'for expansion and general purposes'. Its investment bank sent it back: investors need to know how much goes to the new Bahir Dar plant, how much to working capital and how much repays loans. The revised draft broke the figure into three lines.

worked.title: ECMA offer registration fees compared (Directive No. 996/2024)

rows.label: Share offer of Birr 400 million: 300,000 + 0.1% x 400,000,000
Bond offer of Birr 500 million: 150,000 + 0.05% x 500,000,000
Bank A share offer of Birr 2 billion: 300,000 + 0.1% x 2,000,000,000

worked.note: Bond offers carry a lower fixed fee and half the variable rate of share offers.

lessons.title: Insider dealing, manipulation and false statements
body: The proclamation prohibits three families of market abuse. Insider dealing is trading, or tipping others to trade, on material information that is not public, such as unannounced results or a planned capital raise. Market manipulation is creating a false or misleading impression of price or volume, for example by buying and selling between related accounts or spreading rumors to move a price. False statements are misleading information given to the market or to investors.
Market abuse is prohibited for everyone, licensed or not. It can lead to ECMA sanctions and criminal liability.

left.title: Legitimate
items: Trading on public information and your own analysis
Publishing honest research with conflicts disclosed
Buying because you believe the price is low
Disclosing material news promptly to everyone

right.title: Prohibited
items: Trading before a capital raise is announced
Telling a friend about unannounced results
Trading between your own accounts to fake volume
Posting false rumors to move a price

example.title: The accountant's tip
example.text: Eyerusalem, a senior accountant at a fictional listed brewery, saw that annual profit would fall by half. Before the results were published she told her brother, who sold his shares. Both face insider dealing liability: she for tipping, he for trading on information he knew came from an insider.

scenario.title: The Telegram pump
scenario.situation: Kidus Wondimu runs a 9,000-member Telegram channel. He buys a thinly traded ESX share, posts that a 'big foreign buyer' is coming, then sells when members push the price up 30%. No foreign buyer exists.
scenario.question: How is this activity classified?
options: Prohibited market manipulation and false statements
Permitted, since it is free speech
Permitted if he discloses he owns the share
scenario.explain: Spreading a false story to move a price and selling into the rise is manipulation. Disclosure of his holding does not cure a false statement.

lessons.title: Conflicts of interest and client assets
body: A licensed firm often has interests that differ from its clients': it earns commissions, holds its own positions and may advise the issuer whose shares it sells. The rule is to identify conflicts, manage them, disclose them to clients, and decline the business where a conflict cannot be managed.

Client money and securities belong to clients. They must be held in separate client accounts, never used for the firm's expenses or its own trading, reconciled regularly and reported to clients. If the firm fails, segregated assets go back to clients rather than to the firm's creditors.
points: Identify, record and disclose conflicts
Put the client's order before the firm's own
Segregate client money and securities in designated accounts
Reconcile client accounts frequently and report to clients

example.title: The diaspora client's order
example.text: Bethlehem Tefera, a diaspora engineer in Washington DC, placed an order to buy 500 shares through a fictional Addis Ababa broker. The broker's dealing desk wanted the same shares. Its compliance rules put her order first and recorded the time of both orders, so she got the better price and the firm could show it.

scenario.title: Borrowing client cash
scenario.situation: A fictional broker's finance manager, Tamrat Ayele, is short of Birr 800,000 for salaries. Client cash of Birr 12 million sits in the client account and he plans to borrow from it for three days.
scenario.question: What is the right response?
options: Allow it, since it will be repaid in three days
Allow it if the CEO approves
Allow it if clients are told afterwards
Refuse: client money cannot fund the firm; raise funds from shareholders and report any shortfall in capital
scenario.explain: Client money is not the firm's money for even one day. Using it is a serious breach, whatever the approvals or the repayment plan.

lessons.title: AML/CFT: customer due diligence and beneficial ownership
body: Capital market firms are reporting entities under Ethiopia's AML/CFT law (reported as Proclamation No. 780/2013). Before opening an account, the firm must identify and verify the client, understand the purpose of the account and the source of funds, and identify the beneficial owner: the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a client that is a company, cooperative or trust.

Higher-risk clients, such as politically exposed persons or complex foreign structures, need enhanced checks and senior approval. Suspicious transactions must be reported to the Financial Intelligence Service without tipping off the client. Diaspora and foreign investor funds must also follow the FX rules in FXD/01/2024.

items.label: Identify
items.text: Name, ID (Fayda where available), address

items.label: Verify
items.text: Check documents against reliable sources

items.label: Beneficial owner
items.text: Find the natural persons behind entities

items.label: Risk-rate
items.text: Standard or enhanced due diligence

items.label: Monitor and report
items.text: Watch activity; report suspicion to the Financial Intelligence Service

example.title: A teacher in Adama
example.text: A fictional broker onboarded Almaz Kebede, a secondary school teacher in Adama investing Birr 40,000 of savings. Standard due diligence was enough: Fayda ID, a phone and address check, and a short source-of-funds note. The broker still risk-profiled her and recorded that she wanted long-term growth with low risk.

scenario.title: The reluctant cooperative
scenario.situation: The Sidama Coffee Growers Cooperative Union wants to invest Birr 30 million in ESX-listed shares. Its representative refuses to name the board members and controlling persons, saying 'we are a cooperative, everyone owns it'.
scenario.question: What should the broker do?
options: Open the account, since cooperatives are low risk
Explain that the firm must identify those who control the union, such as its board and signatories, and not open the account until it can
Open the account and ask later
Report the union to the police
scenario.explain: For entities without a single owner, due diligence identifies the natural persons who control them. No identification, no account. Suspicion reporting is a separate decision based on facts.

regulation.source: Ethiopian AML/CFT proclamation (reported as Proclamation No. 780/2013)
regulation.text: Requires reporting entities to carry out customer due diligence, identify beneficial owners, keep records and report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Service. Confirm current CDD directive requirements before training.

lessons.title: Exercise: permitted, licensable or prohibited
body: Here is the Level 1 exercise. For each activity, ask three questions. Is it a capital market activity done as a business? Then it is licensable. Does it deceive the market or misuse inside information? Then it is prohibited. Otherwise it is permitted.
Work through the twelve cases below before reading the answers in brackets. Several look harmless but cross a line.
points: Selling bank shares to 150 people without a prospectus (prohibited unless registered as a public offer)
Advising a diaspora client on ESX shares for a fee (licensable: investment advice)
Running a share-trading Telegram group with paid tips (licensable; prohibited if it spreads false stories)
Buying listed shares for your own savings (permitted)
Holding clients' share certificates and cash for a fee (licensable: custody)
Trading before your employer announces a capital raise (prohibited: insider dealing)
Publishing a university study of ESX liquidity (permitted)
Taking client orders through a mobile app for a broker (licensable: digital sub-broker)
Trading between your own two accounts to show volume (prohibited: manipulation)
Rating a company's bonds and selling the rating (licensable: credit rating agency)
A bank teller referring a depositor to a licensed broker (permitted)
Pooling neighbors' money to buy shares you choose (licensable: fund operation or portfolio management)

scenario.title: The adviser's referral fee
scenario.situation: A licensed broker offers Bank A tellers Birr 200 for each new client they refer. Tellers would hand over a brochure and do not recommend any share.
scenario.question: How is this arrangement best classified?
options: Permitted as a referral if the fee is disclosed and tellers give no advice
Licensable, so each teller needs a broker license
scenario.explain: A pure referral is not advice. Disclosing the fee manages the conflict; the moment tellers recommend specific shares, they cross into advice.

worked.title: Two classifications with numbers

rows.label: Offerees in the bank share sale
ECMA transaction fee on a Birr 400,000 share trade: 0.15%
ECMA transaction fee on a Birr 2,000,000 bond trade: 0.005%

worked.note: Counting offerees decides the classification; fees decide what the client pays. Both are part of everyday compliance work.

takeaways: A public offer must be registered with ECMA with a prospectus; private placements are reported as limited to 100 investors.
A prospectus covers risks, use of proceeds, audited financials, directors and owners, offer terms and holders' rights.
Insider dealing, manipulation and false statements are prohibited for everyone and can bring criminal liability.
Client money and securities are segregated and never used for the firm, even for a day.
Customer due diligence reaches the natural persons behind every client; suspicions go to the Financial Intelligence Service.

quiz.q: A company sells shares to 120 investors without registration, calling it a private placement. What is the issue?
options: It exceeds the reported 100 investor ceiling, so it is a public offer needing registration
It needs only a Commercial Code resolution
quiz.explain: Above 100 investors, the offer is treated as public.

quiz.q: Which is insider dealing?
options: Buying after reading a published annual report
Selling after a director tells you, before publication, that profits will halve
quiz.explain: Trading on material non-public information from an insider is insider dealing.

quiz.q: A client buys Birr 1,000,000 of ESX shares. What ECMA transaction fee applies?
What happens to properly segregated client assets if a broker fails?
options: They go to the broker's creditors
They are shared with the NBE
quiz.explain: Segregation keeps client assets out of the firm's estate.

quiz.q: Who is the beneficial owner of a company client?
options: The natural person who ultimately owns or controls it
quiz.explain: Beneficial ownership looks through entities to the people who own or control them.

quiz.q: Where are suspicious transactions reported?
quiz.explain: Reports go to the Financial Intelligence Service, and the client must not be tipped off.

modules.title: Compliance programs and issuer obligations
modules.summary: Build and run a compliance program for a licensed firm, meet ECMA's reporting calendar, and advise issuers, including widely held unlisted share companies, on disclosure, governance and listing.
objectives: Design a compliance manual, monitoring plan and whistleblowing channel
Meet the reporting deadlines and record-keeping rules of Directive No. 980/2024
Advise an issuer on prospectus liability and continuous disclosure
Apply NBE governance and shareholder approval rules to a bank preparing to list
Test an issuer against the ESX Main Board listing criteria

lessons.title: Building the compliance program
body: A compliance program turns rules into daily habits. It starts with a risk assessment: which rules matter most for this firm's activities, clients and products. From that come a compliance manual of policies and procedures, a monitoring plan that tests whether staff follow them, training, a whistleblowing channel and regular reports to the board.

The program is a cycle, not a binder. Each monitoring finding feeds back into the risk assessment and the manual. A program that has not changed in a year in Ethiopia's fast-moving market is probably out of date.
points: Compliance manual approved by the board
Annual monitoring plan with tests and sample sizes
Whistleblowing channel independent of management
Quarterly compliance report to the board

example.title: Bank A Capital's monitoring plan
example.text: Selamawit Desta built Bank A Capital's first monitoring plan around five risks: client onboarding, order handling, client money, conflicts and reporting. Each month she tests a sample, for example 25 new client files against the due diligence checklist and every client money reconciliation. Findings go to the audit committee every quarter.

lessons.title: Regulatory returns and the reporting calendar
body: Directive No. 980/2024 sets firm deadlines. Quarterly financial statements go to ECMA within 30 days of quarter end. Audited annual accounts go within 90 days of the year end. Breaches must be reported within 24 hours of discovery. Records must be kept for 10 years.
Missing a deadline is itself a breach, and a pattern of late returns tells ECMA that controls are weak. Sanctions under the directive include fines of up to Birr 2 million and suspension.

scenario.title: The Friday evening breach
scenario.situation: At 18:00 on a Friday, Bank A Capital's operations team finds that client money of Birr 1.4 million was paid into the firm's own account by mistake on Wednesday. It was moved back at 17:30.
scenario.question: What should the chief compliance officer do?
options: Nothing, since the money is back
Report the breach to ECMA within 24 hours of discovery and record the cause and fix
Report only if a client complains
scenario.explain: Correcting the error does not remove the duty to report. The 24-hour clock runs from discovery, and the record should show the root cause and the control added.

regulation.source: ECMA Directive No. 980/2024, Licensing and supervision of capital market service providers
regulation.text: Quarterly statements within 30 days of quarter end; audited accounts within 90 days of year end; breaches reported within 24 hours; records kept for 10 years. Sanctions include fines of up to Birr 2 million and suspension of the license.

worked.title: Bank A Capital's compliance calendar, 2026

rows.label: Quarter ending 30 September 2026: statements due (30 days)
Financial year ending 30 June 2026: audited accounts due (90 days)
Breach discovered Thursday 15 October 2026 at 14:00: report due (24 hours)
Client order records from 2026: keep until (10 years)

worked.note: Put every date in a shared calendar with an owner and a reminder at least a week before.

lessons.title: Inspections, sanctions and the gap review
body: ECMA inspects licensed firms on site and through returns. Inspectors test client files, reconciliations, conflicts registers, complaints logs and board minutes. A firm prepares by running its own gap review first: a structured comparison of what the rules require with what the firm actually does.

A gap review lists each requirement, the evidence the firm holds, the gap, the risk and an owner and date for the fix. It is also the work assignment for this course: learners run one on their own firm.

example.title: A gap review that paid off
example.text: Before its first ECMA inspection, a fictional adviser in Hawassa ran a gap review and found that 40 of 160 client files lacked a signed risk profile. It fixed them in six weeks and recorded the remediation. Inspectors noted the self-identified gap and closed it without sanction.

scenario.title: The inspection finding
scenario.situation: ECMA inspectors find that a fictional broker reconciled client money only twice in a year and could not explain a Birr 230,000 difference.
scenario.question: What outcome should the firm expect and prepare for?
options: No action, since the amount is small
A sanction that may include a fine of up to Birr 2 million or suspension, and an order to fix reconciliation
Transfer of supervision to the NBE
scenario.explain: Weak client money controls go to the heart of investor protection. The directive allows fines of up to Birr 2 million and suspension.

lessons.title: Issuer obligations: prospectus liability and continuous disclosure
body: The issuer and those responsible for the prospectus, including its directors and the advisers who sign parts of it, can be liable to investors for material misstatements or omissions. That is why due diligence, verification notes and sign-offs matter.

After listing, issuers report periodically, with audited IFRS accounts annually and interim reports, and continuously: material information that could affect the price must be disclosed promptly to the whole market, not first to friendly analysts. Until it is published, the information is inside information.

items.label: Offer
items.text: Prospectus with full and fair disclosure; liability for misstatements

items.label: Listing day
items.text: Securities admitted to the ESX board

items.label: Every period
items.text: Interim and audited annual IFRS reports

items.label: Any day
items.text: Prompt disclosure of material information to the whole market

example.title: The verification note
example.text: Dawit Gebremedhin, Bank A's legal counsel, required every factual statement in the draft prospectus to be traced to a source: board minutes, audited accounts or NBE correspondence. The statement 'Bank A has 412 branches' turned out to include 9 not yet opened, and was corrected before filing.

scenario.title: A letter from the NBE
scenario.situation: A year after listing, Bank A receives an NBE letter saying its capital will fall below a new requirement unless it raises Birr 1 billion within 12 months. The CEO wants to wait until the half-year results in four months.
scenario.question: What should legal counsel advise?
options: Treat it as likely material information, disclose it promptly to the market and keep an insider list until then
Wait, since the results will explain it
Disclose only if the share price falls
scenario.explain: A required capital raise can move the price. It must go to the whole market promptly; selective disclosure would create insider dealing risk.

lessons.title: Corporate governance of listed issuers and banks
body: Investors pay more for companies they trust. Listed issuers are expected to have independent directors, audit committees, clear related party rules and accounts prepared under IFRS or AABE standards, as the ESX Rulebook requires for listing.
A bank that lists also remains under NBE governance rules, which are often stricter than general corporate rules. Directors and influential shareholders of banks need NBE approval.

example.title: Bank A's board check
example.text: Before filing its listing application, Bank A compared its board against SBB/91/2024. It had 11 directors, 4 independent and 3 women, but one director had served 7 years. The board planned his replacement at the next general meeting so that the prospectus could describe a compliant board.

scenario.title: A director's term
scenario.situation: One of Bank A's directors has served 7 years and is popular with shareholders. The chair suggests keeping him through the listing for continuity.
scenario.question: What should the company secretary advise?
options: Keep him; listing rules do not cover banks
Make him an observer with a vote
Ask ECMA for a waiver of the NBE rule
Replace him at the next general meeting, since SBB/91/2024 sets a 6-year term limit
scenario.explain: The NBE term limit applies regardless of the listing; ECMA cannot waive an NBE rule.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/91/2024, Bank corporate governance; and SBB/89/2024, Persons with significant influence
regulation.text: A bank board has at least 9 directors, one-third independent and at least 2 women, a 6-year term limit and four mandatory committees. Under SBB/89/2024, influential shareholders holding 2% or more, directors, the CEO and senior executives need NBE approval.

lessons.title: Legacy unlisted share companies and bank share transfers
body: Ethiopia has many share companies, especially banks and insurers, with thousands of shareholders but no listing. ECMA rules bring the trading of such shares into a regulated setting: they may list on the ESX or be traded on a regulated over-the-counter market, which sits under ECMA's exchanges and OTC directive (reported as No. 1009/2024), with transition rules for existing companies. Check the current text before advising.

For banks, share transfers have an extra gate: the NBE must approve anyone who would become an influential shareholder at 2% or more under SBB/89/2024. The Commercial Code also gives existing shareholders pre-emption rights on new shares, which a general meeting must respect or waive as the Code allows.

scenario.title: A legacy shareholder's sale
scenario.situation: A fictional insurer with 9,000 shareholders is not listed. A shareholder asks its registrar to record a sale of shares at a price agreed privately through a broker's Telegram notice.
scenario.question: What should the registrar check first?
options: Nothing; private sales are always valid
Whether the trade complies with current ECMA rules for unlisted share trading and the company's transfer rules, and whether the broker is licensed
Whether the price is above par
scenario.explain: Legacy companies now sit in a regulated environment. The registrar checks ECMA's current OTC and transition rules, the articles of association and who intermediated the trade.

worked.title: Does a share purchase need NBE approval? (Bank A, before the raise)

rows.label: Shares he agrees to buy from other holders
Result
rows.value: Crosses 2%: NBE approval needed before the transfer is registered

worked.note: The share registrar should hold the transfer until NBE approval arrives, whether it happens off-exchange or, after listing, through the ESX.

lessons.title: Can Bank A meet the ESX Main Board test?
body: The ESX Rulebook (December 2024) sets two equity boards. The Main Board (Rule 5.1) needs market capitalization or shareholders' equity of at least ETB 500 million on listing, a 3-year track record, a profit after tax at least once in the last 3 years, IFRS or AABE accounts, and a public float of 15% held by at least 300 holders, or 10% if market capitalization is ETB 2 billion or more.

The Growth Board (Rule 6.1) is for younger firms: a 2-year track record, revenue growth of 20% a year, market capitalization of at least ETB 50 million and a 10% float held by at least 50 holders, with no profit test. On both boards insiders may sell at most 50% of their shares within 12 months of listing.

left.title: Main Board (R. 5.1)
items: ETB 500 million market cap or equity
Profit after tax once in 3 years
15% float, 300 holders (10% if ETB 2 billion or more)

example.title: A growth firm's choice
example.text: Gerji Software S.C., a fictional Addis Ababa company, has a 2-year record, revenue growing 35% a year, an ETB 120 million valuation and no profit yet. It fails the Main Board profit and track record tests but fits the Growth Board, provided it places at least 10% of its shares with at least 50 holders.

worked.title: Bank A against the Main Board criteria

rows.label: Profit after tax in the last 3 years (needs once)
Expected market capitalization after the raise
rows.value: ETB 9.6 billion, so the 10% float test applies

rows.label: Shares held by directors and 2%+ holders
Director holding 1,200,000 shares: most he may sell in 12 months (50%)

worked.note: Bank A comfortably meets the Main Board test. The real work lies in disclosure, NBE approvals and preparing 15,000 shareholders for dematerialized trading.

takeaways: A compliance program is a cycle: assess risks, write policies, train, monitor, report and fix.
Directive No. 980/2024 deadlines: quarterly statements in 30 days, audited accounts in 90 days, breaches in 24 hours, records for 10 years.
Issuers and those responsible for the prospectus can be liable for misstatements; material news goes to the whole market promptly.
A listing bank stays under NBE governance rules: SBB/91/2024 for the board and SBB/89/2024 for 2% shareholders.
The ESX Main Board needs ETB 500 million, 3 years, profit once in 3 years, IFRS or AABE accounts and a 15% or 10% float.

quiz.q: Within how many days must a licensed firm send ECMA its quarterly financial statements?
quiz.explain: Directive No. 980/2024 sets 30 days from quarter end.

quiz.q: A breach is discovered at 09:00 on Monday. When is the report to ECMA due at the latest?
quiz.explain: Breaches must be reported within 24 hours of discovery.

quiz.q: What is the maximum fine under Directive No. 980/2024 cited in this course?
quiz.explain: Sanctions include fines of up to Birr 2 million and suspension.

quiz.q: An issuer with market capitalization of ETB 3 billion lists on the Main Board. What minimum public float applies?
quiz.explain: The float drops from 15% to 10% when market capitalization is ETB 2 billion or more.

quiz.q: A buyer would reach 2.5% of a bank's shares. What is required?
quiz.explain: Holders of 2% or more are influential shareholders needing NBE approval.

quiz.q: A loss-making firm with a 2-year record and 25% annual revenue growth wants to list. Which board fits?
quiz.explain: The Growth Board has no profit test and needs a 2-year record and 20% annual revenue growth.

modules.title: Market abuse enforcement, funds and the listing roadmap
modules.summary: Go deeper into surveillance, insider lists, Chinese walls and enforcement across ECMA and the NBE, learn how collective investment schemes are structured and valued, then build Bank A's full regulatory roadmap.
objectives: Set up insider lists, closed periods and Chinese walls in a banking group
Analyze an enforcement case that involves ECMA, NBE and Commercial Code rules
Describe the structure, gatekeepers and disclosure of collective investment schemes
Compute and challenge a fund's net asset value
Map every regulatory step and approval for a bank listing and capital raise

lessons.title: Surveillance and insider lists
body: Exchanges and ECMA watch trading for unusual patterns: sharp price or volume moves before announcements, trades between linked accounts, and orders placed and canceled to mislead. An alert leads to questions to the broker, then to the client.

Issuers help by keeping insider lists: the names of everyone with access to inside information on a project, the date they gained access and an acknowledgment that they know the rules. Many firms also set closed periods before results when directors and key staff may not trade.

items.label: Open the project
items.text: Name it with a code word; restrict documents

items.label: List insiders
items.text: Name, role, date of access, signed acknowledgment

items.label: Close trading
items.text: Insiders barred from trading in the shares

items.label: Announce
items.text: Publish to the whole market at once

items.label: Close the list
items.text: Keep the list as a record for 10 years

example.title: Project Gihon
example.text: Bank A named its listing and capital raise 'Project Gihon'. By the time the prospectus was filed, the insider list held 64 names: directors, executives, Bank A Capital's team, auditors, lawyers and printers. Each signed an acknowledgment, and the list showed ECMA exactly who knew what, and when.

scenario.title: An insider's spouse
scenario.situation: Two weeks before the capital raise is announced, a Bank A executive on the insider list asks whether his wife may buy 2,000 Bank A shares from another shareholder, since she is not on the list.
scenario.question: What should compliance answer?
options: Yes, she is not an insider
Yes, if the trade is off-exchange
No: a trade by a family member using information from an insider is insider dealing, and insiders must not tip or procure trades
Yes, if she pays above par
scenario.explain: The prohibition covers tipping and procuring. Routing the trade through a spouse or off-exchange does not change its nature.

lessons.title: Chinese walls in a banking group
body: In a banking group, one team may hold inside information while another trades or advises. Chinese walls are the barriers that keep it apart: separate teams and floors, restricted document access, a watch list and restricted list kept by compliance, and controlled 'wall-crossing' when a person must be brought inside.

Walls must be real. If Bank A Capital advises Bank A on its own listing while its brokerage desk recommends Bank A shares to clients, the conflict is acute. The group must separate the teams, disclose the relationship in the prospectus and research, and consider an independent co-adviser.
points: Physical and system separation of deal teams
Watch list (confidential) and restricted list (no trading or research)
Documented wall-crossings approved by compliance
Disclosure of group relationships to clients and investors

example.title: The wall-crossing log
example.text: When Bank A Capital needed its head of brokerage, Feven Asrat, to advise on how retail shareholders would trade after listing, compliance logged her wall-crossing, added her to the insider list and barred her from Bank A trading and research until the announcement.

scenario.title: Advising your own parent
scenario.situation: Bank A Capital will be lead adviser on Bank A's listing. Its brokerage desk wants to publish a 'buy' note on Bank A shares to clients during the offer period.
scenario.question: What should compliance require?
options: Allow the note, since research is free speech
Put Bank A on the restricted list for research during the offer, disclose the group relationship and keep the deal team behind the wall
Let the deal team write the note
Send the note only to diaspora clients
scenario.explain: A group firm promoting its parent's offer, possibly with inside knowledge, is a severe conflict. Restricting research and disclosing the relationship manages it.

lessons.title: From alert to sanction: an enforcement case in depth
body: Real cases cross regulators. Take a bank director who sells shares just before bad news. ECMA can investigate the trade as insider dealing under the proclamation, with administrative sanctions and possible criminal liability. The NBE can reconsider whether the director remains fit and proper under SBB/89/2024. The company may act under the Commercial Code and its articles, for example by removing the director at a general meeting.
A good case analysis separates the questions: what each authority can decide, what evidence it needs and in what order the steps run. Measuring the gain made or loss avoided helps size the harm.

example.title: The case timeline
example.text: In the training case, ECMA's alert came from ESX surveillance three days after the announcement. ECMA requested broker records within a week, interviewed the director within a month and issued its decision after a hearing. The director appealed to the Capital Market Tribunal while the NBE separately asked Bank A's board to suspend him pending its fit and proper review.

scenario.title: Which authority does what?
scenario.situation: A Bank A director sold 20,000 Bank A shares the day before the market learned of the NBE capital letter. ECMA has opened an investigation.
scenario.question: Which statement is correct?
options: Only ECMA can act, since the trade was on the ESX
Only the NBE can act, since the director sits on a bank board
ECMA can pursue market abuse, the NBE can review his fitness under SBB/89/2024, and shareholders can act under the Commercial Code
No one can act until a criminal court convicts him
scenario.explain: The same facts raise market abuse, prudential fitness and corporate questions. Each authority acts within its own law.

worked.title: Loss avoided by an insider (fictional listed brewery)

rows.label: Shares sold two days before the profit warning

worked.note: The loss avoided is the measure of the benefit from the inside information and a starting point for the sanction and any recovery the law allows.

lessons.title: Collective investment schemes: structures and gatekeepers
body: A collective investment scheme pools money from many investors and invests it under a stated policy. The operator, or fund manager, makes the investment decisions. An independent trustee or custodian holds the assets and checks that the operator follows the fund's rules. Auditors check the accounts.

ECMA's directives on collective investment schemes (numbers to confirm) set how schemes are approved, what their offering documents and reports must disclose, and how assets are valued and held. Directive No. 980/2024 sets the operator's minimum capital at Birr 25 million and a custodian's at Birr 100 million, reflecting the trust placed in each.

items.label: Investors
items.text: Buy units and receive their share of returns

items.label: Operator
items.text: Manages the portfolio; Birr 25 million minimum capital

items.label: Trustee or custodian
items.text: Holds assets independently; custodian Birr 100 million

items.label: Auditor
items.text: Audits the fund's accounts

items.label: ECMA
items.text: Approves and supervises the scheme

example.title: A balanced fund for teachers
example.text: A fictional teachers' association in Mekelle asked about a fund that would invest members' savings in T-bills and listed shares. The adviser explained the gatekeepers: an ECMA-licensed operator, an independent custodian holding the assets, monthly valuation and an annual audited report.

scenario.title: The operator as its own custodian
scenario.situation: A fictional fund operator proposes to hold the fund's T-bills and shares in its own name to save custody fees.
scenario.question: What should ECMA's licensing reviewer expect instead?
options: Require an independent trustee or custodian to hold the assets in the fund's name
Accept, since the operator is licensed
Let the auditor hold the assets
Allow it if investors are told
scenario.explain: The independent holder of assets is the main protection against misuse by the operator.

regulation.source: ECMA directives on collective investment schemes (reported; numbers to confirm) and ECMA Directive No. 980/2024, Licensing and supervision of capital market service providers
regulation.text: Schemes need ECMA approval, an offering document, an independent holder of assets and regular reports to investors. A scheme operator needs Birr 25 million and a custodian Birr 100 million of cash capital.

lessons.title: Valuing a fund: net asset value and pricing
body: Investors buy and redeem units at the net asset value (NAV) per unit: the market value of the fund's assets, less its liabilities, divided by units in issue. Fair valuation matters because a wrong NAV transfers value between investors who come in and those who leave.

Listed securities are valued at market prices, T-bills at their accrued or market value, and illiquid assets such as unlisted shares by a documented method that the trustee or custodian checks. With a young market, valuation policy needs particular care.

visual.caption: Assets less liabilities, divided by units outstanding.

scenario.title: Pricing unlisted bank shares
scenario.situation: A fund holds unlisted shares in a fictional insurer. The operator wants to value them at the last private sale price of Birr 2,400, a deal between two related shareholders eight months ago.
scenario.question: What should the custodian push for?
options: Use the par value of Birr 1,000
A documented fair value method, such as recent arm's length trades or valuation multiples, reviewed independently
scenario.explain: A stale, related-party price is not fair value. A documented, reviewed method protects both entering and leaving investors.

worked.title: Entoto Balanced Fund: NAV at month end (Birr million)
worked.note: If the operator overvalued the shares by Birr 9 million, NAV per unit would read Birr 1.15, and new investors would overpay.

lessons.title: Capstone: Bank A's regulatory roadmap
body: This is the Level 2 case. Bank A, with 15,000 shareholders, plans to list on the ESX and raise Birr 2 billion of new capital. Teams map every step and approval from ECMA, the ESX and the NBE and draft the compliance timeline. The roadmap is 40% of the assessment.

A strong roadmap orders the steps by dependency, names the authority and document for each, and flags the gating items: the NBE approvals, a complete prospectus and shareholders ready to hold dematerialized shares. Confirm the current ECMA public offer and OTC rules and any NBE notification requirements before relying on any timeline.

items.label: Months 1 to 2
items.text: Board decision; appoint advisers; NBE approval for Bank A Capital under SBB/92/2024; Bank A Capital applies for its ECMA license

items.label: Months 2 to 4
items.text: Due diligence; IFRS audited accounts; governance fixes under SBB/91/2024; insider list opened

items.label: Months 4 to 5
items.text: General meeting under the Commercial Code: capital increase, pre-emption, listing

items.label: Months 5 to 7
items.text: Prospectus registered with ECMA; ESX Main Board application; fees paid

items.label: Months 7 to 8
items.text: Offer period; allocation; NBE approval for any subscriber reaching 2%

items.label: Month 9
items.text: Shares dematerialized at the CSD; listing on the ESX; continuous disclosure begins

example.title: The team's critical path
example.text: One training team found that the longest chain in Bank A's roadmap was not the prospectus but shareholder readiness: about 3,000 of the 15,000 shareholders had outdated addresses and no Fayda ID. They added a shareholder update campaign in months 2 to 6, run through the branches, so that holdings could be moved to the CSD before listing.

scenario.title: What comes first?
scenario.situation: Bank A's CEO wants to announce the offer price and open subscriptions next month to catch strong demand. The general meeting has not met, the prospectus is not registered and Bank A Capital has no license yet.
scenario.question: What should the roadmap show as the next step?
options: Open subscriptions now and register later
Hold the general meeting and complete registration with ECMA before any offer is made to the public
Announce the price on social media only
Ask the ESX to waive registration
scenario.explain: No public offer can be made before ECMA registration, and the share issue needs a general meeting resolution. Announcing early also risks misleading the market.

worked.title: Bank A roadmap: approvals and owners

rows.label: NBE: bank investment in Bank A Capital (SBB/92/2024)
ECMA: investment bank license for Bank A Capital (Directive No. 980/2024)
General meeting resolution on the capital increase
ECMA: offer registration and prospectus; fee ETB 2,300,000
Post-listing: disclosure calendar and insider policy

worked.note: Every line has an authority, a document and an owner. Gaps in ownership are where timelines slip.

lessons.title: Work assignment: a compliance gap review of your own firm
body: The Level 2 assessment adds a work assignment worth 20%: a compliance gap review of your own firm. The test is 30% and participation 10%, alongside the 40% roadmap. The suggested pass mark is 70%.

Use the structure from Module 4: list the requirements that apply to your firm, the evidence you hold, the gap, the risk rating, the fix, the owner and the date. Keep it factual and confidential, and present the top five gaps to your manager.
points: Scope: licensing conditions, capital and liquid assets, people, client assets, conflicts, AML/CFT, reporting, records
Evidence: documents, samples and dates, not opinions
Rating: high, medium or low, by impact on investors and on the license
Plan: owner, date and how you will test the fix

items.text: Pick the rules that apply to your firm

items.label: Evidence
items.text: Collect documents and test samples

items.label: Rate
items.text: High, medium or low risk

example.title: A broker's top five gaps
example.text: Ruth Getachew, a compliance officer at a fictional broker, found five high-priority gaps: client money reconciled weekly instead of daily, no closed period for directors, three client files without beneficial owner records, a conflicts register last updated a year earlier, and no 24-hour breach procedure. Each had an owner and a date within 60 days.

scenario.title: Rating a gap
scenario.situation: In her review, Ruth finds that the firm's records are kept for 5 years and then deleted to save server space.
scenario.question: How should she rate and fix this gap?
options: High risk: the rule is 10 years, so stop deletion immediately, recover what is possible and change the retention policy
Ask clients to keep their own records
scenario.explain: Directive No. 980/2024 requires 10-year record keeping. Ongoing deletion destroys evidence, so it is high risk and needs immediate action.

takeaways: Insider lists, closed periods and surveillance make insider dealing harder to commit and easier to prove.
In a banking group, Chinese walls, restricted lists and disclosure manage the conflict when a subsidiary advises its parent.
One set of facts can trigger ECMA market abuse action, NBE fitness review and Commercial Code steps at the same time.
A fund needs an operator, an independent trustee or custodian, fair valuation and honest NAV; a wrong NAV moves value between investors.
A listing roadmap orders steps by dependency, names an authority, document and owner for each, and is confirmed against current rules.

quiz.q: What is an insider list?
options: A list of a company's largest shareholders
A record of everyone with access to inside information on a project, with dates
quiz.explain: It records who knew what, and from when.

quiz.q: What does a restricted list do in a banking group?
options: Bars trading or research in named securities while the group holds sensitive information
quiz.explain: Restricted lists stop activity that would exploit or appear to exploit inside information.

quiz.q: A fund has assets of Birr 330 million, liabilities of Birr 30 million and 250 million units. NAV per unit?
Who should hold a collective investment scheme's assets?
options: The operator in its own name
quiz.explain: Independent custody protects investors from misuse by the operator.

quiz.q: An insider sold 10,000 shares at Birr 800 before bad news; the price then fell to Birr 650. Loss avoided?
In the Level 2 assessment, what weight does the regulatory roadmap carry?
quiz.explain: Roadmap 40%, test 30%, gap review 20%, participation 10%.

exam.q: A share company plans to raise Birr 900 million from the public. What ECMA registration fee should it budget?
exam.explain: ETB 300,000 plus 0.1% of 900 million (ETB 900,000) equals ETB 1,200,000.

exam.q: An ESX procedure conflicts with Directive No. 980/2024, which in turn seems to conflict with the proclamation. Which rule governs?
exam.explain: Higher rules prevail: the proclamation ranks above directives, which rank above exchange rules.

exam.q: An agricultural company sells 'profit certificates' to 250 farmers, promising a share of profits from a processing plant the company runs. What is the best first assessment?
options: A bank deposit for the NBE
A likely security offered to the public, needing review and probably ECMA registration
A cooperative matter outside any law
exam.explain: Pooled money, returns from another's efforts and more than 100 investors point to a public offer of securities.

exam.q: Founders of a proposed dealer have Birr 8 million in cash and a Birr 4 million building. Can they meet the dealer minimum?
options: Yes, the total is Birr 12 million
Yes, dealers need only Birr 6 million
Yes, if the building is debt-free
No, they need Birr 10 million in cash
exam.explain: A dealer needs Birr 10 million, paid in cash; the building does not count.

exam.q: A broker has total assets of Birr 80 million and liquid assets of Birr 30 million. What is its position?
options: Short by Birr 2 million against the 40% minimum
exam.explain: 40% of Birr 80 million is Birr 32 million; Birr 30 million falls Birr 2 million short.

exam.q: A bank with total capital of Birr 10 billion already holds Birr 1.3 billion of non-bank equity. It wants to invest another Birr 300 million in a non-bank company that is not a capital market firm. What does SBB/92/2024 suggest?
options: It fits, since the limit is Birr 2 billion
It would breach the 15% aggregate limit of Birr 1.5 billion
exam.explain: 15% of Birr 10 billion is Birr 1.5 billion; 1.3 plus 0.3 billion is 1.6 billion.

exam.q: A bank wants to rate corporate bonds for investors and also to broker shares directly from its branches. What does SBB/92/2024 allow?
options: Both, as part of banking business
Neither directly: it may own up to 100% of a broker subsidiary with NBE prior approval, but may not act as a service provider itself or hold equity in a credit rating agency
Both, if ECMA licenses the bank
exam.explain: The bank works through a licensed subsidiary for brokerage and is barred from holding equity in a credit rating agency.

exam.q: A firm's chief compliance officer resigns, leaving two appointed representatives. What is the issue?
options: Only the NBE must be told
It falls below the minimum of three appointed representatives including a licensed chief compliance officer, and must appoint and notify promptly
It must surrender its license at once
exam.explain: Directive No. 980/2024 requires at least three, including a licensed chief compliance officer.

exam.q: An issuer offers shares to 90 investors in March and to another 70 in April on the same terms for the same project. What is the compliance concern?
options: The rounds look like one offer to 160 investors split to avoid the reported 100 investor ceiling
exam.explain: Splitting one offer to stay under the private placement ceiling defeats the rule.

exam.q: A client sells Birr 3 million of shares and buys Birr 4 million of government bonds through the ESX. What ECMA transaction fees apply in total?
A trader buys and sells the same thinly traded share between his and his brother's accounts all day. Which classification fits?
exam.explain: Trades between linked accounts that create false volume are manipulation.

exam.q: A company client's representative will not identify who controls it. The broker's best course is:
options: Open the account with enhanced monitoring
Not open the account until the controlling natural persons are identified, and consider whether a suspicion report is warranted
Open it if the deposit is under Birr 1 million
Tell the client a report has been filed
exam.explain: No beneficial owner, no account; tipping off is prohibited.

exam.q: A firm's financial year ends 30 June. By what date must its audited accounts reach ECMA?
exam.explain: 90 days from 30 June is 28 September.

exam.q: During a pre-listing review, a bank board has 9 directors, 2 independent and 2 women. Under SBB/91/2024, what must change?
options: It needs at least 3 independent directors, one-third of 9
exam.explain: One-third of 9 directors is 3 independent directors.

exam.q: A bank has 8,000,000 shares. An investor holds 120,000 and wants to buy 50,000 more. What follows?
options: No approval, the holding stays below 2%
NBE approval is needed, since 170,000 is 2.13%

exam.q: A company has ETB 1.2 billion market capitalization, a 4-year record and one profitable year in the last three. What Main Board float does it need?
exam.explain: Below ETB 2 billion, the Main Board float is 15% held by at least 300 holders.

exam.q: A listed company learns that a major contract worth a third of its revenue has been canceled. What is the right step?
options: Disclose promptly to the whole market and control insiders until then
Disclose only if the price falls
exam.explain: Material information goes to the whole market promptly; selective disclosure creates insider dealing risk.

exam.q: Bank A Capital advises Bank A on its listing while its brokers want to recommend Bank A shares. Which control is most appropriate?
options: None, since the group is one company
Let brokers share the deal team's model with clients
Restrict research on Bank A during the offer, keep deal staff behind a Chinese wall and disclose the relationship
Move the deal team to the brokerage floor
exam.explain: Walls, restricted lists and disclosure manage the group conflict.

exam.q: A fund reports assets of Birr 500 million including unlisted shares at a stale price Birr 20 million above fair value, liabilities of Birr 5 million and 450 million units. What is NAV per unit after correcting the shares?
exam.explain: Corrected NAV = (500 minus 20 minus 5) / 450 = 475 / 450 = Birr 1.06 (rounded).

exam.q: In Bank A's roadmap, which step must come before any public subscription opens?
options: ECMA registration of the offer and prospectus, after the general meeting resolution
exam.explain: No public offer can be made before ECMA registration, and the issue needs a general meeting resolution first.
